items.title: Two Ways In Before the Holiday Rush: Exploited Adobe Commerce Flaws Put Online Stores at Risk
items.summary: Two actively exploited Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-48356 and CVE-2026-75650) are giving attackers code execution on ecommerce store servers just as holiday shopping season begins. This entry breaks down how each attack works and what store operators should do to patch and check for compromise.

items.title: Racing the Update: Attackers Probe a WordPress Core Flaw That Opens During Patching
items.summary: Attackers are probing CVE-2026-119977, a WordPress Core flaw that opens only during a core update. Here’s how the race works, why the severity ratings disagree, and how to protect your sites.

items.title: TrendAI Vision One™ extends Claude integration
items.summary: AI agents are now acting on your endpoints. TrendAI Vision One™ ingests Claude Code and Cowork session records so your team can review what users asked Cowork to do, all in the same console.

items.summary: On 20 October at 15:20 UTC, a Hacker News post leaked details of two critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow remote code execution. The post was removed, but screenshots circulated on X and Mastodon.

items.summary: Eight eMudhra intermediate CA keys were compromised, some as weak as 3 bits. Learn the code-signing risk and the steps to hunt for misuse and close the gap from TrendAI™.

items.summary: Two critical PHP flaws leaked before patches shipped, and the same day Mozilla disclosed weak eMudhra certificate authority keys. In this post, TrendAI™ Global CISO Sundari Parekh gives security leaders a practical playbook.

items.summary: Earth Sirrush has repeatedly changed its tools and delivery methods, but TrendAI™ Research reveals how shared code, reused artifacts, and infrastructure patterns continue to expose the links between its campaigns.

items.title: Inside SHADOW-WATER-084: A Steganographic Loader-as-a-Service Delivering Remcos, LXBASE, and More
items.summary: TrendAI™ Research tracked three campaigns that ship completely different decoy applications and unrelated payloads, all riding one shared toolkit. This analysis covers the full chain, from the pixel data that hides the first stage, through a flexible shared loader to deliver multiple payloads, revealing how adversaries are standardizing their delivery mechanisms.
